quote: The page is on the middle of the bridge when a barge horn blasts below
why: R1 (6:40) the page is already 'crossing the bridge', R2 'still crossing', R3 (6:48) 'still on the far side of the bridge, getting smaller'. By 6:55 he is back at the middle; fifteen minutes on one bridge and the position goes backwards.

quote: ride on to Thornhallow tonight to say it was done. He's lodging for the night at the Drowned Candle, an inn on the near bank, and is meant to leave at dawn.
why: Same paragraph says Tobin rides to Thornhallow tonight and that he stays the night and leaves at dawn.

quote: He lets slip that he came upriver from Marrowford the same day you did
why: R18 Tobin says of the same man 'He came to the kitchens yesterday, asking for work', i.e. the day before Wren arrived. Also Thornhallow is downriver of Marrowford, not upriver.

quote: He can't do it in front of twelve pairs of eyes.
why: Only a cook, a pot-boy and a kitchen-maid are in the room (R21 mentions a cook and a boy).

quote: "Aldous married Maud Fenn," he says. "My grandmother. I remember her hands.
why: R13 Edric believed the grandsire's marriage was into the Aldermere house and only 'half-suspected' it was false. He remembers his own grandmother as flour-scented Maud Fenn, so he would have known she was no Aldermere.

quote: an hour or two of start ahead of you and a team of horses to your mule
why: The fishwife in the same scene says the wagon left 'at dawn' and it is 1:30 PM, so the start is about seven hours (R27 then says 'hours ahead').

quote: he sat up all night over that brass lamp over my door
why: R28 Marta says of that same lamp 'He gave that lamp over the door'. If Corvin gave it he would not study it on his first stay. R33 Hob says Elowen left it over the door twenty years ago.

quote: Garrow comes splashing across the shallows with his short blade
why: R40 had Garrow with 'a short sword under his coat', but the game rolls 'Garrow's scimitar attack'.

quote: Your Intimidation check was a 3
why: The dice line shows [3] + 3 = 6; the narration reports the bare die as the check result.

quote: you send Kit to the driver, and he comes back with a dead man's belt-pouch
why: Kit is 'he' here and 'she' from R46 on ('a stocky... woman', 'Kit ... she').

quote: The little iron key fits.
why: R2: the hairpin snapped, 'leaving a sliver of metal wedged in the keyway', so the lock is jammed. No one clears it, yet the key opens it.

quote: You sleep in the same small room under the eaves
why: The eaves room was at Thornhallow (R25). At Thistlewood Wren had a guest room with bed, table, pen and candle (R38).

quote: chain mail, a shield, a longsword, a light crossbow
why: In R42-R44 Kit fights with a spear and no shield is mentioned.

quote: you still owe the hall your account at noon
why: In the same reply the arbiter says she will hear Wren 'this afternoon'; R67 then sets 2 PM.

quote: for twenty years he hasn't touched it
why: Elowen died sixteen years ago (R83) and Wren is about 19, so the staff cannot have sat untouched twenty years. In R71 Corvin also says the keeper 'showed me the door', so he did try to claim it.

quote: vs watcher's passive Perception 12
why: Sparrow's passive Perception is 13 in R78 and R81.

quote: You could also hurl something else, such as the flask of oil at your belt
why: In R90 Wren threw her only flask of oil up to Brann (sheet: lost 1 x Oil), and R93's notes say Brann used 'Wren's lamp-oil'.

quote: Brann kept the light dark by her word and waited for the lantern-foot.
why: In R80 Ysolde says the light has been dark fifteen years 'since the channel moved and the ships stopped coming'. The two reasons and dates differ.

quote: The squall arrives just as the skiff pulls clear.
why: In R85 Brann said the squall would come 'by afternoon, hours yet'; here it hits around 8:20 AM.

quote: It names *H.* as a Master Hale, now held at Thornhallow.
why: Corvin's own hidden note (R74) says 'H. watches the east door' of the Wick-House. A man held in a Thornhallow cellar (R75) cannot be doing that.

quote: You were four, perhaps five.
why: Wren is about 19 (R70 'nineteen years'), which would be 14 to 15 years with Corvin. The player-stated 'nineteen years' in R70 was never corrected. Annis (R105) describes the girl as small enough to sleep on a shoulder.

quote: She came back once, at midwinter, and held you all night.
why: In R94 Brann says Elowen reached the spit alone in the autumn, fevered, and died there that winter. Annis has her fevered at Rushlight the same autumn and alive at midwinter, which doesn't fit.

quote: where his horse is a dark mile away
why: Earlier the watcher sat the dike 'a quarter mile off' (R106) and the horse waits 'beyond the crest' (R109).

quote: The twentieth is a long way off
why: In R102 the DM ruled that the assize at month's end is the 30th.
